newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close mostly higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mostly higher after an afternoon of volatile, active trade ahead of options expirations on Friday, traders and analysts said.
"This is going to be one for the books," one stock analyst said about Friday's expiration of January options on equity indexes.
"Unless we see something in the earnings picture to rattle the market, stocks are headed higher," said Jeff Feeney, vice president at Smith Barney.
Positive corporate earnings fueled the Dow Industrials' climb, as well as the Nasdaq and Standard & Poor's 500s, analysts and traders said.
The strong earnings scenario overshadowed the U.S. bond market, which sharpened losses throughout the day.
U.S. bonds weakened in reaction to comments from Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer, who said that consumer prices, excluding volatile food and energy, could rise in 1997.
U.S. bonds tumbled on the comments, and pushed March S&Ps through the minor support level of 772.00.
"Locals really wanted to push the market lower," one trader said.
Before long, March S&Ps fell through the pivot point of 771.90 and through Wednesday's settlement of 771.65.
However, the contract found good support at 769.20.
"The resiliency is really remarkable," a floor trader said.

Daniel Riley, director of institutional trading at Chicago Execution Corp, said the market turned short-term oversold at the daily low. One large U.S. firm was a heavy buyer on the downside and an active seller on the upside.
Feeney said Nasdaq 100 futures will be one of the closest indexes to monitor following Microsoft's earnings report.
"It's a great index to play against those two stocks," Feeney said, referring to Microsoft and Intel, which make up a third of the Nasdaq 100 index.
Fair value for March S&Ps was at 4.70 over cash.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 3.60 at 775.25, NYSE Composites were up 1.70 at 408.80, KCBT Value Lines were 3.55 higher at 703.90, Nikkeis were down 275.0 at 17,950, Midcap 400s were 1.60 higher at 265.80, and Nasdaq 100s rallied 12.45 to 883.60.
